title: Protocol for using fluorescent sensors targeted to endogenous proteins (FluoSTEPs) to measure microdomain-specific signaling events
protocol: Plate HEK cells in 6-well plates at approximately 50% confluency.
Transfect each well with 1 μg of px459 plasmid encoding the customized gRNA and 20 pmol of ssDNA ultramer HDR template using Polyjet, following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Passage cells from each well into separate 60-mm dishes.
Prepare a puromycin selection curve with concentrations of 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 μg mL−1.
Choose the lowest concentration of puromycin that achieves 99% cell death by day 3 for selection.
Add 1 μg mL−1 puromycin to each 60-mm dish one day after passaging.
Exchange media for puromycin-free media when no viable cells remain in the non-transfected dish (around 2–3 days).
Passage and resuspend cells in FACS sorting buffer, including DAPI.
Sort for DAPI-negative cells with the expected size using FACS.
Plate single cells into a 96-well plate with media containing 15 mg/L phenol red and 20% FBS.
Stain puromycin-selected cells with DAPI.
Subject DAPI-stained cells to FACS to identify the DAPI− cell population.
Single-cell sort DAPI− cells into 96-well plates for cloning and sequencing.
Transfect gene-edited and wild-type cells with a GFP1-10 expression plasmid one day prior to FACS.
Culture cells after sorting GFP+ cells using FACS.
Perform another round of FACS to select GFP− cells to avoid genomic integration of GFP1-10.
Sort single-cell colonies into wells for expansion.
Passage single-cell colonies.
Keep half of the colonies for further expansion in 6- or 12-well plates using normal FBS concentrations.
Use the other half of the colonies for genomic DNA extraction with a kit such as the DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Qiagen).
Perform PCR on the extracted genomic DNA using a kit such as the Q5 High-Fidelity Kit (New England Biolabs) and primers designed to amplify the target region of the GOI.
Gel extract PCR products using a kit such as the PureLink Quick Gel Extraction kit (Invitrogen).
Clone gel-extracted PCR products into TOPO PCR vectors.
Subject cloned PCR products to Sanger sequencing for evaluation of copy number of correct gene edits.
Passage cells that are identified to have successful knock-in, as well as wild-type cells, into 35-mm glass-bottom dishes at approximately 30% confluency.
Transfect 1 μg of GFP1-10 plasmid into both knock-in and wild-type cells via PolyJet 1 day after passaging.
Image cells 1 day after transfection.
Aspirate the cell media without touching the bottom of the dish.
Wash twice with 1 mL of HBSS.
Add 2 mL of HBSS for imaging.
Mount the imaging dish on the microscope stage and image in the GFP channel.
Use the GFP1-10-transfected wild-type cells as a guide for determining the autofluorescence background signal.
Reconstitute poly-D-lysine in sterile water at a concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Coat the 35-mm glass-bottom dish with 400 μL Poly-D-Lysine (PDL).
Incubate the dishes with PDL for 30 min in a sterile, 37°C incubator.
Wash the dishes 3 times with sterile PBS in a biosafety cabinet.
Let the coated dishes dry for 30 min in a biosafety cabinet.
Wrap the dried dishes in parafilm and store at 4°C.
Passage FP11-cells.
Transfect cells 1 day later with 1 μg of the FluoSTEP probe of your choice.
Image cells 1 day after transfection.
Prepare drugs at 1000× stock concentration.
Aliquot 2 μL of 1000× drug stocks into separate 1.5 mL tubes.
Store drug aliquots properly during imaging, typically on ice.
Select appropriate excitation and emission filters for monitoring GFP and RFP fluorescence intensities.
Adjust gain settings as needed for optimal signal detection.
Choose an ND filter (e.g., 0.3 ND) to minimize photobleaching.
Set exposure times (e.g., 500 ms) for the FRET and GFP channel.
Determine image acquisition interval (e.g., 30 s).
Select a high-magnification objective lens (e.g., ≥40×) for detailed imaging of subcellular structures.
Image cells in three channels: green direct, red direct, and green-red FRET.
Acquire images for at least 5 minutes to establish baseline signal before drug addition.
Pause the imaging cycles.
Use a P1000 micropipette to transfer approximately 0.5 mL of HBSS from the imaging dish into a 1.5 mL tube containing an aliquot of 1000× drug stock.
Mix briefly in the 1.5 mL tube.
Carefully add the HBSS + drug mixture back to the imaging dish.
Mix at least three times in the imaging dish to ensure homogeneous distribution of the drug.
Pipet gently and away from the center of the dish to avoid displacing cells from the surface.
Avoid directly touching the imaging dish when performing drug addition to prevent shifting the microscope field of view.
Restart the imaging cycles and image the cells until the fluorescence signal reaches a stable plateau.
Image the cells for at least 5 minutes before the first drug addition.
Repeat imaging for subsequent drug additions.
